result:
Solution 2 is the only candidate that can be correct, and I rate that confidence as moderate.

Solutions 1 and 3 are refuted by Solution 2's construction, which I checked. Take any plane triangulation B on w vertices, insert a vertex p_f into each face f, then insert q_f adjacent to p_f and two corners of one subface. The result is a triangulation on n = 5w − 8 vertices. The inserted vertices induce only the matching edges p_f q_f, so every P_3 must use a vertex of B. Hence λ_{P_3}(G) ≤ w = (n+8)/5, which gives c ≤ 1/5. Since 1/5 < 1/4 < 1/3, the claimed values 1/3 (Solution 1) and 1/4 (Solution 3) cannot be the liminf. Solution 3's lower-bound theorem is also unsupported.

I did not verify the matching lower bound c ≥ 1/5. Solution 2's counting argument only shows that one type of obstruction forces |W| ≥ (n+8)/5. A full proof would need to rule out other packing obstructions. I believe the value 1/5 matches the known result for this problem, but I have not confirmed that from a source.

CHOICE: 2
CONFIDENCE: 3
